'''Sixth Heaven Shrine''' (第六天神社, Dairokuten Shrine) refers to various shrines located mainly in the {{ill|Kantō region|en|Kantō region|qid=Q132480|lt=Kantō region}} and nearby areas of Japan. Some variations of the name, such as "大六天" (Dairokuten), are also used by certain shrines.
== History and Characteristics ==
The Sixth Heaven shrines originated during the period of {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|ja|神仏習合|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto-Buddhism Syncretism|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2279088}} (神佛結合), originally dedicated to the {{ill|Demon King of the Sixth Heaven|ja|第六天魔王|lt=Demon King of the Sixth Heaven (Dairokuten Maō)}} (天魔 or {{ill|māra|ja|魔羅|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mara|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 魔|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 魔|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q15726943}}) of Buddhist cosmology. However, following the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ca|Shinbutsu bunri|de|Shinbutsu-Bunri|es|Shinbutsu bunri|fa|شینبوتسو بونری|fi|Shinbutsu bunri|fr|Shinbutsu bunri|id|Shinbutsu bunri|it|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離|ru|Симбуцу бунри|tr|Şinbutsu-bunri|zh|神佛分離|qid=Q1970535|lt=Separation of Shinto and Buddhism}} during the Meiji Restoration, many of these shrines reinterpreted their deities, replacing them with the sixth generation of deities in {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}} and {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書経}} ({{ill|Omodaru and Ayakashikone|ja|面足|lt=Omotaru}} and {{ill|Ayakashikone|ja|惚根}}).<ref group="Note">As per {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書経}}, these deities are written as 面足命 and 惚根命, respectively. {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}} provides different representations as 氌母阠神 and 阿夜赁志古泥神.</ref>
According to the journal *Japanese Folklore No. 127*, historical records show over 500 shrines named "Sixth Heaven Shrine" by the late {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}: 320 in {{ill|Musashi Province|en|Musashi Province|qid=Q907398|lt=Musashi Province}}, 140 in {{ill|Sagami Province|ja|相鮮国}}, and 40 in {{ill|Izu Province|en|Izu Province|qid=Q860928|lt=Izu Province}}.<ref name="Folklore127">*Japanese Folklore No.127*, March 1980, article by Hiroshi Kimura, "Development of Sixth Heaven Belief."</ref> However, due to the aforementioned separation policy, many were renamed, merged, or reduced to subsidiary shrines. Currently, only 36 registered independent shrines remain.<ref name="ShrineGuide">*Kanagawa Shrine Guidebook*, 1997, Kanagawa Shrine Association.</ref>

Folklore suggests this distribution resulted from {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|ja|筒田信長}}'s reverence for the Sixth Heaven Demon King, which led {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|qid=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}} to suppress the associated shrines west of {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|en|Nagano Prefecture|qid=Q127877|lt=Nagano Prefecture}}.<ref name="ShrineGuide"/>
== Deities and Unique Cases ==
While most Sixth Heaven shrines have adjusted their deities, some exceptions exist. For instance:
* {{ill|Takagi Shrine|ja|高木神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takagi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q45072661}} in {{ill|Sumida, Tokyo|en|Sumida, Tokyo|qid=Q235135|lt=Sumida, Tokyo}} worships {{ill|Takamimusubi|ja|高木神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takagi no Kami|qid=Q125400|qid=Q125400|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q125400}}.
* {{ill|Dairokuten Shrine (Natori, Miyagi)|ja|名古第六天神社}} remains tied to {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|ja|天の緊尾神}} ({{ill|Omodaru and Ayakashikone|ja|面足|lt=Omotaru}} and {{ill|Ayakashikone|ja|惚根}}).
* {{ill|Dairokuten Shrine (Iwaizumi, Saitama)|ja|埼玉県稲草区第六天神社}} has notable links to {{ill|Sky Fox (mythology)|en|Sky Fox (mythology)|qid=Q11442920|lt=Tengu}} folklore.<ref>Local legend connects its deity with protective {{ill|Sky Fox (mythology)|en|Sky Fox (mythology)|qid=Q11442920|lt=Tengu}} spirits, featuring unique effigies.</ref>

== Major Sixth Heaven Shrines (第六天神社) ==
The following is a list of notable shrines with the name "Sixth Heaven" (第六天 or 大六天) that still exist today. These shrines are predominantly found in the {{ill|Kantō region|en|Kantō region|qid=Q132480|lt=Kantō region}}, though they can also be seen in the {{ill|Tōhoku region|en|Tōhoku region|qid=Q129465|lt=Tōhoku region}} and parts of the {{ill|Chūbu region|en|Chūbu region|qid=Q134638|lt=Chūbu region}} (including {{ill|Kōshin'etsu region|ja|甲信越|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōshin'etsu|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 甲信越地方|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 甲信越地方|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q398208}}<ref name="dairokuten-koushinetsu">Reference: [https://ameblo.jp/soubu-nakamiti/entry-11978770465.html Kōshin’etsu and Jōetsu Dairokuten Map] (Exploring Dōsojin and Dairokuten).</ref> and {{ill|Tōkai region|en|Tōkai region|qid=Q398989|lt=Tōkai region}}, specifically {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|en|Shizuoka Prefecture|qid=Q131320|lt=Shizuoka Prefecture}}). However, west of {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|en|Nagano Prefecture|qid=Q127877|lt=Nagano Prefecture}} and Shizuoka Prefecture, these shrines are scarcely found.
According to {{ill|Company register|en|Company register|qid=Q1394657|lt=corporate registry}}, there are 36 registered religious corporations with names that include variations of "Sixth Heaven": 19 as "Dairokuten Shrine," 4 as "Dairokuten Sha," 1 as "Dairokuten Miya," 2 as "Dairokusha," 5 as "Dairokuten Shrine" (using the kanji 大六天), 3 as "Dairokusha" (大六天社), and 2 as "Maōten Jinja." None of these include place names in their official titles. For instance, {{ill|Musashi Dairokuten Shrine|ja|武蔵第六天神社}} and {{ill|Dairokuten Sakaki Shrine|ja|第六天榊神社}} are officially registered as simply "Dairokuten Shrine" and "Sakaki Jinja," respectively. Shrines with religious corporation status are marked with a ☆ below.

* {{ill|Dairokuten Shrine (Sendai)|ja|大六天神社 (仙台市)}} ({{ill|Sendai|en|Sendai|qid=Q46747|lt=Sendai City}}, {{ill|Aoba-ku|en|Aoba-ku|qid=Q904456|lt=Aoba-ku}}, Ōkura)
; Fukushima Prefecture
* {{ill|Dairokuten Maō Jinja (Kōriyama)|ja|大六天魔王神社 (郡山市)}} ({{ill|Kōriyama|en|Kōriyama|qid=Q264206|lt=Kōriyama City}}, Tamuramachi, Kanazawa Dairoku) Known as "Maō Shrine" - The shrine's signboard displays "Dairokuten Maō Jinja," while the torii bears the name "Maō Shrine."<ref>[https://ameblo.jp/miyamoto-gotoh/entry-12650137834.html Dairokuten Maō Shrine Goshuin, Kōriyama City, Tamuramachi] (Ameba Blog: Shrine Pilgrimages, January 14, 2021).</ref>
